conventions: Wayland Dispatch pattern uses event_created_child! for child proxy events
crate::session::is_wayland() at runtime to select backend
Option<OwnedFd> for fd fields that may not be populated
Wayland state mutated directly via Dispatch (no Arc<Mutex>)
Proxy .id() returns u32 — stable identifier for HashMap keying

hard: No transient wl_surfaces created for clipboard ops (causes Mutter taskbar blinking)
Wayland clipboard reads must not call arboard (creates per-call Wayland connections)
WaylandState is !Send — external Mutex provides thread safety
image::load_from_memory blocks — must not hold Tauri IPC lock during decode
ExtDataControlSourceV1 must be explicitly .destroy()'d or orphaned proxies leak compositor resources
GTK clipboard read (get_text_via_gtk) must run on main thread only
soft: Prefer additive changes over invasive refactors
Match existing code patterns for Wayland access (see get_current_text pattern)
MIME type comparisons should be lenient (real compositors vary whitespace/case)
Multi-seat: current impl uses devices[0] — document as OK for v1
compatibility: Must work on GNOME/Mutter (ext_data_control), KDE/KWin, Sway (wlr-data-control)
Must fallback to wl-copy + GTK when ext_data_control not available

patterns: Event-driven: WaylandState as Dispatch target, mutated via event_queue roundtrip
Pipe-based fd transfer: offer.receive(write_fd) -> compositor writes -> read from read_fd
Three-stage read: roundtrip -> dispatch -> read from stored fd -> cache in state
Preference chain: ext_data_control > GTK (main thread) > arboard > external tools
Wayland writes: create source -> offer MIMEs -> store text -> set_selection -> flush
Fallback chain for set_text_robust: native Wayland -> wl-copy -> arboard

gotchas.text: ExtDataControlSourceV1 proxy must be explicitly .destroy()'d — Wayland protocol objects live on queue until destroyed or connection drops; orphaned proxies leak compositor-side resources
Proxy .id() returns u32 that is unique per object lifetime — safe HashMap key. Verified via wayland-client source: ObjectId is monotonically increasing per connection.
image::load_from_memory can be expensive (decode + allocate) — working tree fix already ensures decode runs outside wayland_clipboard borrow, but Mutex is still held
wl-copy external process creates transient wl_surfaces triggering Mutter assertions — the whole point of adding native ext_data_control write path
Current working tree has uncommitted changes for A, E, F, B (partial), G, H, I — must verify before building on top

prior_decisions.decision: Use ext_data_control_v1 instead of wl-copy/arboard for Wayland clipboard reads
rationale: Avoids per-call Wayland socket connections causing Mutter assertions
Eliminates transient wl_surfaces that cause taskbar blinking on GNOME/Mutter

prior_decisions.decision: Extend to writes: use ext_data_control_v1 for set_text_robust as primary path
rationale: Same benefits as reads — no transient surfaces, no taskbar blink
WaylandClipboard::set_text() already exists but was never wired
Falls back to wl-copy then arboard for robustness

prior_decisions.decision: Generation counter over bool+deadline for owns_selection
rationale: Deadline is a heuristic — gen counter is deterministic
Each set_text gets unique gen count, Selection handler compares directly
DataOffer/Cancelled events properly reset per-seat expectation

prior_decisions.decision: Per-source HashMap over VecDeque for pending text
rationale: Event::Send receives a specific source proxy — HashMap keyed by source.id() is exact match
VecDeque assumes FIFO order which may not match compositor event ordering
Each source's text is independently tracked, no ordering ambiguity
